questions.question: Which of the following describes the speed of an object at a particular moment?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Instantaneous speed. Instantaneous speed is the speed of an object at a specific point in time or at a particular instant.

questions.question: The gradient of a distance–time graph is calculated by:

options.A: Dividing the change in distance by the change in time
options.B: Multiplying the change in distance by the change in time
options.C: Taking the square root of the sum of the squares of distance and time
options.D: Dividing the change in time by the change in distance

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Dividing the change in distance by the change in time. Slope or gradient is "rise over run." In a distance-time graph, the rise is the change in distance and the run is the change in time, representing speed.

questions.question: The slope of a velocity–time graph represents:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity (a = \Delta v / \Delta t), which corresponds to the slope of a velocity-time graph.

questions.question: The area under a velocity–time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Displacement. The product of velocity and time represents the change in position, which is displacement.

questions.question: If the velocity–time graph of a body is a horizontal straight line, the motion is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Uniform velocity. A horizontal line means the velocity value is constant and not changing over time.

questions.question: A velocity–time graph is a straight line inclined to the time axis. This indicates:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Uniform acceleration. A straight inclined line shows that velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time, which is uniform acceleration.

questions.question: If a body moves with negative acceleration, the velocity–time graph will:

options.A: Be parallel to the time axis

questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Incline downward. Negative acceleration (deceleration) means velocity is decreasing over time, causing the graph to slope downwards.

questions.question: Terminal velocity is attained when:

options.A: Net force on the body is zero
options.D: Weight of the body becomes zero

questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Net force on the body is zero. Terminal velocity occurs when the upward drag force equals the downward weight, making the net force zero.

questions.question: When a raindrop falls through air, it attains terminal velocity because:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Air resistance balances its weight. As speed increases, air resistance increases until it equals the weight of the drop, preventing further acceleration.

questions.question: At terminal velocity, the acceleration of a falling object is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Zero. Since velocity becomes constant at terminal velocity, the change in velocity (acceleration) is zero.

questions.question: Terminal velocity depends upon:

options.B: Shape and size of the object

questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Density of the medium. Mass affects weight, while shape, size, and medium density affect the drag force; all determine the speed at which balance is reached.

questions.question: If the velocity–time graph is below the time axis, the body is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Moving backward (negative velocity). The region below the time axis represents negative velocity values, indicating motion in the opposite direction.

questions.question: Which of the following quantities cannot be obtained directly from a velocity–time graph?
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Distance. On a velocity-time graph, displacement is the net area, acceleration is the slope, and initial velocity is the intercept at t = 0. Total distance requires taking the absolute value of areas if motion changes direction, so it cannot be read directly.

questions.question: For a skydiver after jumping from a plane, terminal velocity occurs when:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Weight = Air resistance. Terminal velocity occurs when the downward force of gravity (weight) is balanced by the upward force of air resistance, resulting in zero net force and zero acceleration.

questions.question: A body moving with terminal velocity has:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Zero acceleration but finite velocity. It moves at a constant, non-zero speed (finite velocity) with no change in that speed (zero acceleration).

questions.question: If an object moves in a straight line and returns to its starting point, its:

options.A: Speed is zero but velocity is not
options.B: Velocity is zero but speed is not
options.C: Both speed and velocity are zero
options.D: Neither speed nor velocity is zero

questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Velocity is zero but speed is not. When an object returns to its starting point, its net displacement is zero (so average velocity is zero), but total distance travelled is non-zero (so average speed is not zero).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true regarding average acceleration?

options.A: It is the total change in velocity divided by the total time
options.B: It gives an average rate of velocity change over a period
options.C: It represents the acceleration at a specific point in time
options.D: It can be zero even if instantaneous accelerations are non-zero

questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): It represents the acceleration at a specific point in time. Acceleration at a specific point in time is called "instantaneous acceleration," not average.

questions.question: Distance covered by an object in a distance–time graph is represented by:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): The height of the graph. The y-coordinate (height) on a distance-time graph directly tells you the distance covered up to that time.

questions.question: is the study of motion of an object.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Mechanics. Mechanics is the branch of physics that deals with the motion of physical objects and the forces that affect them.

questions.question: If a body does not change its position with respect to its surrounding, then it will be in the state of .
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): rest. Rest is defined as the lack of change in position relative to a chosen reference point or surroundings.

questions.question: If a body changes its position with respect to its surrounding, then it will be in the state of .
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): motion. Motion is the continuous change of position of an object compared to its surroundings.

questions.question: Rest and motion of a body is .
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): relative. An object may be at rest for one observer (like a passenger in a car) but in motion for another (someone on the sidewalk).

questions.question: The motion of a body about an axis is called. .
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Rotational. When every point of a body moves in a circle around a fixed line (axis), it is rotatory or rotational motion.

questions.question: A body has translator motion if it moves along :
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): line without rotation. According to FBISE Class 9 textbook, in translatory motion, a body moves along a line without any rotation. The line may be straight or curved.

questions.question: The motion of aeroplanes flying straight in the air is:
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Linear motion. Movement along a straight line is specifically called linear (or rectilinear) motion.

questions.question: The motion of a gas or liquid molecules along a zig-zag path is called.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): Brownian motion. The irregular, zig-zag motion of gas or liquid molecules (particles suspended in a fluid) is called Brownian motion (or random motion).

questions.question: is the motion of a cradle and string of guitar.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Vibratory motion. The back and forth motion of a body about a mean position (like the motion of a cradle or a plucked guitar string) is vibratory (oscillatory) motion.

questions.question: Mass is a quantity.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Scalar. Mass has no direction; you don’t say “5kg to the left.”

questions.question: Force is a _______ quantity.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Vector. Force always acts in a specific direction, which significantly changes the outcome of the physical action.

questions.question: A vector quantity is represented by______

options.C: bar or arrow over their symbol

questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): All of them. These are all standard notation styles used in physics to distinguish vectors from scalars.

questions.question: Shortest distance between two points is known as
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): displacement. Displacement is a vector that points from the starting position to the ending position.

questions.question: Displacement is a quantity.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): vector. Because it specifies a change in position in a specific direction.

questions.question: By dividing the displacement of moving body with time we get
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): velocity. By dividing displacement by time (v = d/t), we get velocity.

questions.question: Acceleration of a body is
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): negative. Also known as retardation or deceleration. 56.Acceleration of a body is if its velocity increases. (a) negative (b) positive (c) uniform (d) variable Explanation: Acceleration is in the direction of motion.

questions.question: If velocity of a body changes equally in equal interval of time then its acceleration is .
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): uniform. A body has uniform acceleration if it has equal changes in velocity in equal intervals of time, however short the interval may be (FBISE textbook definition).

questions.question: If the direction of motion of a body and direction of acceleration of body is same then acceleration will be .
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): Positive. Velocity increases, resulting in positive acceleration.

questions.question: If motion of body is in a interchangeable.

options.B: curved path then distance and displacement, speed and velocity are

questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): straight line. In a one-way straight line, magnitude of distance equals displacement. 63.Slope of a line represents: (a) speed (b) velocity (c) acceleration (d) displacement Explanation: On a V-T graph, the slope is acceleration. (Note: On a Distance-Time graph, it is speed).

questions.question: is the value of g at sea level.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): all of them. The acceleration due to gravity g at sea level is 9.8 m/s² in SI units, 980 cm/s² in CGS units, and 32 ft/s² in British engineering units. All represent the same physical value.

questions.question: If a body is falling under the gravity its initial velocity will be ______.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): zero. An object dropped from rest starts at speed 0.

questions.question: If a ball is dropped from the top of the tower, the distance covered by it in the first two second is. .
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 20m. Using s = 1/2 g t² with g = 10 m/s² and t = 2 s: s = 0.5 × 10 × 4 = 20 m.

questions.question: Uniform velocity with which a paratrooper coming down is also called ______.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): terminal. The constant speed reached when air resistance equals weight.

questions.question: Motion of a wheel is .
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): rotatory. It spins around a central axis.
